missionPremise: P-293 (dispatch _dispatches/2026-09-16_p293-verdict-vocabulary_dispatch.md, dispatched in 6ad2ad35): hauska-factory P-201 (merged at factory 9171279, migration 0011a) widened parcel_gate_verdict's verdict CHECK constraint from pass|refuse|excluded to also admit excluded-not-applicable, excluded-mid-cutover and excluded-no-acquisition-path. LDT's verdict reader accepts only the first three, so once the factory scheduler writes an excluded-* string to a SLATED (county, rail) pair, resolveAllowlistState resolves that pair to legacy instead of the refused it resolves to today for plain 'excluded' - a serve-state change nobody decided, invisible because today's live rows are still plain 'excluded'.

driftTracedAtSource.method: Read at source, not from the dispatch's prose: the four LDT files on this lane's own branch at 62e7349b, plus hauska-factory's merged migrations at 91712795ea2a1eb7c27f7328cf7f52fcb7810b59 (== factory main, read via the GitHub API) and hauska-engine's services/retrieval-api at its own main.

site1_ldt_reader.quoted: export type ParcelGateVerdictKind = "pass" | "refuse" | "excluded"; ... function isVerdictKind(v: string): v is ParcelGateVerdictKind { return v === "pass" || v === "refuse" || v === "excluded"; } ... if (!isVerdictKind(row.verdict)) return null;
site1_ldt_reader.observed: An excluded-* verdict fails isVerdictKind, so loadParcelGateVerdict returns null. The comment there reads 'null means: no usable verdict'. Silent: no log, no distinct return, and the same null a missing row and a query error produce.

site2_ldt_allowlist.quoted: if (!PARCEL_RECORD_SLATE.has(slateKey(countyFips, railKey))) return "legacy"; if (!verdict) return "legacy"; if (verdict.verdict === "pass") return "record"; return "refused";
site2_ldt_allowlist.observed: The allowlist is already correct for any RECOGNISED non-pass string: plain 'excluded' -> refused, 'refuse' -> refused. The drift is entirely upstream of it, in the reader's predicate. This is why the fix belongs in the vocabulary/predicate and NOT in the decision function - and why 'do not change what a pass or refuse verdict serves' is satisfiable with no edit to the decision table at all.

site3_engine_store_narrowing_LIVE_PATH.observed: THE FINDING THAT CORRECTS THE DISPATCH'S OWN MECHANISM. In production the verdict string does not reach LDT's predicate at all. resolveVerdictStore(undefined) -> parcelRecordQueryableFromEnv() -> an HTTP call to the retrieval service; the service's own loadGateVerdict applies the SAME three-string narrowing and returns null for an excluded-* row; LDT's adapter maps that null to an empty row set at parcelRecordCellRead.ts:230 (`if (verdict === null) return { rows: [] as unknown as T[] };`); loadParcelGateVerdict sees no row and returns null; the allowlist resolves legacy. So the customer-visible drift is real, and it happens one hop EARLIER than the dispatch says, in a repo this lane does not own. hauska-engine's services/retrieval-api/src/server.ts:509-544 returns the store result verbatim - it does not narrow - so parcel-record-db.ts:160 is the single upstream narrowing site.

driftTracedAtSource.what_this_means: Two silent narrowings of one vocabulary, in two repos, both collapsing to the same word (null) that both callers document as 'no usable verdict'. Fixing the LDT one is necessary (it is this repo's copy, and it is the copy that would go on dropping a string the engine ever does forward) but it is NOT sufficient for the customer path while parcel-record-db.ts:160 stands. Reported rather than papered over, per DEV_PROCESS 3.2.
